gray._500_origin: Milestone 11 audit. gray.600 measures 3.88:1 on background.primary, 3.36:1 on surface.card and 3.09:1 on surface.cardHover — below WCAG AA's 4.5:1 floor for normal-size text. packages/tokens/README.md has said so since Milestone 3, and three files (detail-stats, deferred-page-notice, and the README itself) had already worked around it individually — while eight others still painted captions, meta lines, legends and a search placeholder in it. gray.500 is the missing step: the same blue-shifted neutral (B = R + 6) lightened until it clears 4.5:1 on the DARKEST surface it can land on (cardHover, 4.56:1), so it is safe on every surface in the system rather than on most of them. gray.600 keeps its documented role — disabled text, decorative rules and icons, where only the 3:1 non-text floor applies.

radius._origin: md=10px CANONICAL (Ch.18 Buttons §4). lg=16px CANONICAL (Ch.19 Cards §4/§5: 'one step larger than Chapter 18's button radius of 10px'). none/sm/xl/full remain INTERIM, derived from Ch.5's 4px base rhythm pending a future consolidated Radius chapter (per Ch.18 §16 and Ch.19 §16's own documented limitations).

opacity._origin: Keys follow Ch.39's own explicit naming ("core.opacity.400" for the disabled value) — a per-mille-style scale, not literal percentages. 100/720/800 (10%/72%/80%) are sourced from Ch.3 border.default and Ch.10 glass-nav/glass-backdrop. 400 (40%) is CANONICAL — Ch.39 §4/§5, the new disabled-state token, exposed as semantic.opacity.disabled. No token for fully-opaque (1) — that's CSS's own default.

breakpoint._origin: Design System Bible Ch.8. This is the single canonical source for these numbers. It IS emitted as a CSS custom property (readable via getComputedStyle/JS), but CSS cannot reference var() inside an @media condition without a preprocessor (ADR-0003 deliberately rejected one) — every @media rule in the codebase must hardcode these exact px values and may cite this token as its source of truth.
